catalog_quote: Concerning the unit of stress within the nucleus of the phonological word and the feature of length found within the corpus of data used for this analysis, stress is predictable as occurring on the first lengthened vowel or, if there are no long vowels, then word initially. ... However, the most efficient analysis was to interpret length as environmentally predictable on all stressed syllables other than word initial (see Level 5). But six data occurred which seemed to nullify this allophonic statement about lengthened vowels; initial syllables were found both lengthened and stressed. ... A minimal pair was discovered with the only difference being the contrast of initial syllable lengthened and stressed versus stressed only. ['sar] stomach ['sa·r] type of shark ... audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation, the phonological-word template and the Level 5 length rule are all verbatim in the held Abbott 1985 PDF/txt at the stated pages (346-347, 342, 352). Deciding source: a 1985 Pacific Linguistics phonology article (35 pp) by the SIL fieldworker, the only phonology of Murik in Glottolog's 22-item bibliography; StressTyp2/Hayes 1995 are downstream of it. The coding 'weight-hedged' (stress on first long vowel else initial, one stress per word, with the hedge that Abbott's preferred analysis makes length derived from stress and marks stress orthographically) matches the source's own stated indeterminacy, so no recode is indicated. Not 'well-sourced' because the source is explicitly tentative and no later dedicated description exists to confirm it; not 'at-risk' because nothing found contradicts it. Best candidate for improvement is Foley 2018 (paywalled area
